text.p: Providence Energy Corp and Southern Energy Inc, a subsidiary of Atlanta-based Southern Co, have agreed to form a new company to sell natural gas and electricity to New England clients, company officials said Wednesday.
"It will hopefully offer one-stop shopping for customers. It will be their choice whether to buy natural gas or electricity from us," Jay Oates, a regional director of Southern Energy, told Reuters.
The new limited liability company, to be named Providence Southern Energy, will be headquartered in Providence, where Providence Energy is based, the companies said in a prepared release.

Oates said ongoing deregulation in both the natural gas and electricity markets inspired the joint venture between Providence, a natural gas retailer, and Southern, the largest electricity producer in the United States.
He said Providence Energy Services, a Providence Energy Corp subsidiary that sells natural gas and electricity throughout New England, "will be swept into this new entity.
"Its customers and employees will become the customers and employees of the new entity," he said.
The new venture will sell energy to residential, commercial and industrial customers, and offer energy consulting and unified billing, the statement said.
"Working together in New England, our two companies can become one of the top retail energy marketers in the region," said Tom Boren, President and Chief Executive Officer of Southern Energy.

Southern Co is the parent firm of five southeast U.S. electric utilities - Alabama Power, Georgia Power, Gulf Power, Mississippi Power and Savannah Electric. It sells energy to nine countries across four continents.
Its Southern Energy Inc. subsidiary provides power and gas marketing and energy trading services throughout North America.
